Real captures of claude TUI panes (golden corpus)
=================================================

Source: claude CLI **2.1.212** (measured 2026-07-17). The raw output of
`tmux capture-pane -p`, kept exactly as it came out. Because these are the real thing
rather than hand-typed strings, a change in the footer/spinner behaviour can be read off
as a diff.

Why the real thing is needed
----------------------------
State detection (spinnerActive / atPromptFooter in tmuxx.go) depends on claude's TUI
strings, a display that is neither a contract nor version-managed, and it had broken three
times as of 2026-07-17 (79b582b -> deac672 -> fce5c5e). All three times the unit tests
stayed green: hand-typed fixed strings never talk to the real CLI, so they say nothing when
the CLI changes. This corpus replaces that hand-typing with measured frames.

**Limit (important)**: this is a lock, not a drift *detector*. If the CLI drifts a fourth
time these tests stay green. Detecting that requires actually running the real CLI,
re-capturing this corpus and reading the diff (P1: the TUI footer contract probe). When you
re-capture on a new CLI version, replace the files here and review the difference.

How they were taken (the re-capture procedure)
----------------------------------------------
A control probe was set up, a real turn was run, and the pane was sampled every 0.5s:

    tmux new-session -d -s probe -x 200 -y 50 -c <scratch dir> "claude"
    # dismiss the folder-trust dialog with Enter
    (for i in $(seq 1 100); do tmux capture-pane -p -t probe > frame_$i.txt; sleep 0.5; done) &
    tmux send-keys -t probe "<prompt>"; sleep 1; tmux send-keys -t probe Enter

Points that matter:
- **Start the sampler before submitting the prompt.** Waiting for go test to start in
  between loses the whole turn (which once nearly led to the wrong conclusion that nothing
  was broken).
- **Watching panes of the live fleet is not enough.** They are all long, token-heavy turns,
  so the token-less spinner (busy_thinking_no_tokens below) never appears and the real
  cause stays hidden.
- The footer differs per mode, so capture manual / plan / bypass separately.

The files
---------
busy_thinking_no_tokens.txt    The thinking spinner "✢ Tempering… (6s · thinking with high
                               effort)" = **no token segment**. Exactly the regression
                               fce5c5e fixed. The old spinnerRe required tokens, so of the
                               100 frames of the 14-second turn containing this frame, 0
                               were judged busy.
busy_tokens_early.txt          Just after tokens appear: "✻ Wibbling… (3s · ↓ 28 tokens)".
busy_tokens_glyph_asterisk.txt Later in the same turn, an example where the glyph changes
                               to "*": "* Wibbling… (14s · ↓ 101 tokens)" = the glyph is
                               not fixed.
idle_manual_mode.txt           Idle in the default (manual) mode. The footer is "⏸ manual
                               mode on · ← for agents" and **has no (shift+tab to cycle)**.
                               Exactly the regression where the old AtIdlePrompt kept
                               returning false.
idle_bypass_bg_shell.txt       Idle under bypass with a background shell running. The hint
                               is pushed out by "· 1 shell ·" = the hint slot is
                               context-dependent.
idle_bypass_hint.txt           Idle under bypass (the plain case, with the hint showing).
idle_plan_mode.txt             Idle in plan mode.
idle_post_turn_summary.txt     The after-the-turn summary "✻ Sautéed for 20s". Past-tense
                               verb, no "…", no parentheses, and **no tokens however long
                               the turn was** (confirmed even on a 13m53s turn). Must not
                               be misjudged as busy.
modal_plan_approval.txt        The plan approval dialog. **The mode footer disappears with
                               it**, so the absence of the footer is itself the signal that
                               a dialog is up. Note that "Would you like to proceed" wraps
                               at 80 columns, so in practice it is "to approve" that is
                               matched (a width-dependent fragility).
modal_folder_trust.txt         The folder-trust dialog at startup (matched on "Esc to
                               cancel").
agents_rail_main_selected.txt  A background agent is running and the input box is bound to
                               **main**. A rail of "● main / ◯ <agent>" appears below the
                               footer. The spinner is "✻ Waiting for N background agents to
                               finish" = no "…" and no parenthesised timer, so it does not
                               read as busy and main reads as plain idle (which is correct
                               in itself).
agents_rail_agent_selected.txt The same session with **the agent side selected**. Only the
                               rail's circles invert (◯ main / ● <agent>); the input box
                               and the footer look identical. Characters typed in this
                               state become **an interruption to that agent**, not part of
                               the main conversation. Demonstrated with the probe: right
                               after typing, "1 queued" appeared on the rail line and the
                               text landed only in the agent's transcript, never in the
                               main conversation (the same shape as the 2026-07-30 sannme2
                               misdelivery). The pane's spinner belongs to the agent, so
                               IsBusy becomes true and pollutes the "the pane is moving"
                               evidence used for delivery verification — this frame pins
                               that too.
agents_rail_navigating_main.txt   Right after opening the rail selection with ↓. **The mode
                               footer is replaced wholesale by "↑/↓ to select · Enter to
                               view"**, so an implementation that looks for the bottom edge
                               by the footer goes blind here (which is why the ruled line is
                               used instead). The cursor always sits on the first row, main.
agents_rail_navigating_agent.txt  The same rail selection with the cursor moved to the agent
                               row and opened with Enter (the frame title changes to the
                               agent name).
agents_home_screen.txt         The **agents home screen** reached by pressing ← from the
                               conversation. The input box placeholder is "describe a task
                               for a new session", and typing here **creates a new session**.
                               The footer is "⏵⏵ bypass permissions · enter to return · …";
                               the mode display's "on" is gone, so atPromptFooter comes off
                               too. Esc returns to the conversation, as the hint says.
modal_rate_limit.txt           The `/rate-limit-options` menu after a turn was cut off by
                               the usage limit (claude 2.1.220, measured 2026-07-31). The
                               turn is over, yet it stops waiting for a human keystroke and
                               **the menu never goes away by itself**. It contains "Esc to
                               cancel" and replaces the input box together with the mode
                               footer, so AtIdlePrompt is permanently false = self-healing
                               misses forever and the session sticks at "in progress"
                               (measured at about 16 hours; docs/log/47 §4-3). The banner
                               "You've hit your session limit …" is transcript text, so it
                               stays on screen even after the menu is dismissed = it must
                               not be used as evidence. **This is the only frame taken from
                               a live fleet pane** (a control probe cannot deliberately hit
                               the limit). Per the convention below, the conversation body
                               was replaced with harmless dummy text and the repository name
                               was masked. Only the structural parts — the menu, the ruled
                               lines and the spinner row — are kept.

Getting back from the agents view to the main conversation (measured; used by LeaveAgentsView)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- When the rail is bound to an agent: **↓ -> Enter -> ↑**. ↓ opens the rail selection with
  the cursor on the first row (main) / Enter returns to main's view / ↑ on the first row
  closes the rail selection. Characters typed afterwards were confirmed to land in the main
  transcript.
- On the agents home screen: **Esc**.
- Do nothing while a draft is left in the box (Enter during rail selection was confirmed not
  to send, but if the display had drifted, sending something a person was still writing
  would be unrecoverable). Measured: with a draft present composerEmpty=false and no
  recovery is attempted.

Notes
-----
- **The five agents_* frames are control probes on claude 2.1.220** (2026-07-30). One
  background agent (`sleep 150`) was run, and the rail operations, the agent view and the
  agents home screen were walked through in order. The rail's circles are U+25CF (selected)
  / U+25EF (unselected), and the input box row is "❯ + U+00A0" — an emptiness test that
  assumes TrimSpace depends on that NBSP.
- Everything else was also taken from **a control probe set up for the purpose**. Panes of
  other sessions in the live fleet show real work, so they are not put into the corpus.
- Only the email address inside the welcome box was replaced with dev@example.com (replaced
  with the same width so the frame's columns do not shift). Everything else is raw.
